answer_text: Osmosis refers to the passive diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane. Textbooks often group this kind of material under human biology or general biology. Water moves from the side with lower solute concentration (higher water potential) to the side with higher solute concentration (lower water potential), continuing until the concentrations equalize on both sides. This kind of question often comes up in introductory life-science courses. This is why plant root hair cells can absorb water from the soil, since the soil water has a lower solute concentration than the cell sap.
